author: NorthEast News Desk
body: European Central Bank policymaker Gabriel Makhlouf warned that substantial additional interest-rate increases could impose meaningful costs on economic growth. The governor of Ireland's central bank said a prolonged Middle East conflict may keep inflation elevated, leaving officials to balance price stability against the risk of tightening financial conditions too far.

The ECB raised borrowing costs Thursday for the second time in 2026. Reuters reported that policymakers may consider another move in October, although no decision has been made. Makhlouf's comments highlight a widening tradeoff: energy-driven inflation can justify restraint, but higher rates also raise financing costs for households and businesses and can suppress investment and demand.

Markets will use incoming inflation, wage and activity data to judge whether further increases are likely. Makhlouf did not argue that the inflation threat has passed; his warning centered on the cumulative effect of going much further. For investors, that means the next policy meeting will turn not only on headline inflation but also on evidence that the euro-area economy can absorb another increase without a sharper slowdown.
dek: Ireland's central-bank governor said prolonged Middle East conflict may sustain inflation, but additional tightening carries increasing economic costs.
headline: ECB policymaker warns further rate hikes could damage growth
